At current spending, that's a structural deficit — but with Lake Trust gone, the spending floor drops by $772/month, which nearly closes the gap. Childcare ran $1,500 this month (elevated). The household still cycles paycheck-to-paycheck within each period despite adequate total income.

reads.macro_connection:
Jackson Hole was the inflection event. Warsh told markets the Fed may 'have work to do' — September hike odds jumped from 40% to 68%. The 10Y pushed to 4.75% (highest since Jan 2025) and 30Y mortgages hit 6.66%, approaching the 2026 peak of 6.69%. Your fixed 3.75% is the most valuable position on the balance sheet — the 291bp spread to market is locked and widening.

The Lake Trust payoff is well-timed. If the Fed hikes in September, the household's rate exposure shrinks to whatever variable-rate component exists in Synchrony and Chase. The eliminated Lake Trust payment no longer transmits rate risk. Your credit union's 4.01% APY held — if the Fed hikes, checking APY may follow upward, one of the rare cases where a hike benefits you directly.

CPI at 3.4% was a reprieve from June's 3.5%, but US-Iran tensions are pushing oil back up. August CPI (releasing Sep 11) may reverse the trend. Real yield on checking stays positive but thin at +0.6%.
reads.monthly_note: August 2026 was the month the household deleveraged. Lake Trust — a recurring presence in every prior statement — is paid off. That eliminates ~$772/month in debt service, the single largest structural improvement in the dataset. Combined with Synchrony and Chase at $144/month, total non-mortgage debt service drops from $916 to $144. The $772/month freed is real cash flow: $9,264/year that can redirect to savings, investment, or liquidity cushion. The month itself was noisy. A one-off Guida paycheck at $2,944 (vs the usual ~$1,590) inflated income to $8,617 — normalize that and income was ~$7,263. Childcare ran $1,500, dining hit a dataset high of $800 (boosted by a northern Michigan road trip through Interlochen, Traverse City, Houghton Lake, and Grayling around Aug 17-21), and Home Depot spending at $429 suggests an active project. Investment transfers dropped to $444 (RH Brokerage only, no Schwab) — the lowest savings rate in the dataset at 5.2%. The intra-month liquidity pattern persisted: checking bottomed at $86 on 08/05 and $198 on 08/19, both rescued by Charter Township paychecks. The household runs three paycheck-to-paycheck micro-cycles within each month. Forward outlook — structurally improved. Normalizing for the one-off Guida check, a standard four-paycheck month generates ~$7,673 in income. Prior months at similar income (May at $7,382, June at $7,469) ran deficits of -$1,576 and -$2,510 respectively. But those months carried ~$300-770 in Lake Trust payments. Removing $772/month in Lake Trust from the spending floor drops a normalized month's outflows from ~$9,337 to ~$8,565 — which against $7,673 in income is still a -$892 deficit. To reach breakeven at the normalized income level, monthly spending needs to drop to ~$7,700. The most actionable levers: childcare (establish baseline — is $1,500 the norm or elevated?), dining ($800 → $500 saves $300), groceries ($1,200 → $1,000 saves $200). If childcare normalizes to ~$800 and dining drops $200, the household approaches breakeven in a standard-income month and runs surpluses in any three-paycheck month from either source.
